query: For HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy, earlier studies separately examined tensile creep at 1250 °C, microhardness changes during cold rolling, elastic moduli from 293 to 1100 K, and hardening after aging at 600–800 °C. However, these findings do not provide a unified explanation of the alloy’s stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior. Thermal expansion is also relevant because mismatch can produce thermal stresses during composite solidification and potentially affect strength. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain the unresolved behavior? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the governing cause, observations predicted relative to a baseline, the relevant temperature and response boundaries, how the earlier findings support the hypothesis, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The high‐temperature strength, low‐temperature hardening, and anomalous thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr refractory high‐entropy alloy all derive from fine, coherently strained intermetallic nano‐precipitates formed during mid‐temperature aging; the thermal expansion mismatch between these precipitates and the bcc matrix generates residual internal stresses that impede dislocation motion across the entire 293 K–1250 °C range.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, homogenized HfNbTaTiZr single-phase bcc solid solution with no detectable intermetallic precipitates
generation.intervention: Isothermal aging at 700 °C for 24 h versus no aging
generation.conditions: Mechanical tests performed between 293 K and 1250 °C under stresses up to 200 MPa; microstructure characterized at room temperature
generation.structural_mediator: Volume fraction, size, and coherency strain of aging-induced nano-scale intermetallic precipitates
generation.mechanism: Mismatch in thermal expansion between coherent precipitates and the bcc matrix produces internal residual stresses that act as obstacles to dislocation glide and climb, enhancing creep resistance, work hardening after cold deformation, and elastic modulus
generation.predicted_outcome: Aged samples will exhibit a significantly lower steady‐state creep rate at 1250 °C (e.g. 20–30 % reduction), a higher elastic modulus at 1100 K (∼10 % increase), and increased microhardness after 50 % cold rolling (∼15 % increase) compared to unaged baseline
generation.baseline: Unaged, as-cast sample with homogeneous bcc microstructure
generation.boundary: Applicable for aging treatments between 600 °C and 800 °C for 12–48 h and mechanical testing from 293 K up to 1250 °C under stresses ≤200 MPa
generation.uncertainty: Kinetics of precipitate formation (composition, volume fraction, size distribution) and the precise magnitude of internal stresses remain uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of HfNbTaTiZr specimens—one unaged, one aged at 700 °C for 24 h. Characterize precipitate population and coherency strain by TEM; measure thermal expansion by dilatometry; conduct tensile creep tests at 1250 °C under 150 MPa; measure elastic modulus from 293 K to 1100 K via ultrasonic pulse; perform microhardness after 50 % cold rolling.
measurements: precipitate size, volume fraction, coherency strain (TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If aged samples show no coherent precipitates with measurable thermal mismatch or exhibit less than 10 % change in creep rate, elastic modulus, and microhardness relative to unaged samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
